record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Long-range Bell violation in vacuum correlations
record.original_question: In quantum field theory, vacuum fluctuations can maximally violate CHSH-Bell inequalities for suitable spacelike separated observables, with the violation tending to zero as the localization regions move apart. For a massive scalar free relativistic Bose field, is some nonzero Bell-inequality violation still possible for regions at arbitrarily large separation?

evidence.quote: It is well known [SW] that vacuum fluctuations maximally violate the CHSH-Bell inequalities for suitable spacelike separated observables, and that this violation goes to zero as the two localization regions are moved apart.
Decide whether some (necessarily small) violation of the inequalities is possible for regions arbitrarily far apart. For definiteness, consider a massive scalar free relativistic Bose field.
But the problem as stated above remains open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a free massive scalar relativistic Bose field on Minkowski spacetime, with mass $m>0$, realized in the algebraic framework of local quantum physics: to each open bounded region $\mathcal{O}\subset\mathbb{R}^{1,3}$ one associates a von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{O})$ of local observables acting on the Fock vacuum Hilbert space, and the vacuum vector state $\omega_0$ is a translation-invariant state on the quasi-local algebra. For a pair of spacelike separated regions $\mathcal{O}_1,\mathcal{O}_2$ with $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{O}_1)\subset\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{O}_2)'$, define the CHSH correlation functional
$$\beta(\omega_0;\mathcal{O}_1,\mathcal{O}_2)\;=\;\sup\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl|\omega_0\bigl(A_1(B_1+B_2)+A_2(B_1-B_2)\bigr)\bigr|,$$
where the supremum is over all self-adjoint $A_i\in\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{O}_1)$, $B_j\in\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{O}_2)$ with $\|A_i\|,\|B_j\|\le 1$. A Bell-CHSH violation occurs iff $\beta>1$. It is known that for suitable spacelike separated $\mathcal{O}_1,\mathcal{O}_2$ one has the algebraic maximum $\beta=\sqrt{2}$, and that $\beta(\omega_0;\mathcal{O}_1,\mathcal{O}_1+a)\to 1$ as a spacelike translation $a$ tends to infinity.

Question: does there exist, for every $R>0$, a pair of bounded spacelike separated regions $\mathcal{O}_1,\mathcal{O}_2$ whose mutual spacelike distance is at least $R$ and for which $\beta(\omega_0;\mathcal{O}_1,\mathcal{O}_2)>1$? Equivalently, can the CHSH inequality be violated by vacuum correlations of the free massive scalar field across regions of arbitrarily large spacelike separation?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface the original Summers–Werner results (maximal vacuum CHSH violation for suitable spacelike separated local algebras, exponential decay of the maximal violation with mass times spacelike distance for massive free fields) and recent (2024–2026) work giving explicit test-function constructions and studying CHSH violation in diamond regions. None of these sources state that the specific question—existence of strictly nonzero Bell-CHSH violation at arbitrarily large spacelike separation for the free massive scalar vacuum—has been definitively resolved. The exponential-decay bound on the maximal violation does not by itself settle whether the violation remains strictly above the local bound at all distances. Status is therefore taken as unknown/likely still open.

status_evidence.title: Maximal violation of Bell's inequalities is generic in quantum field theory
status_evidence.snippet: Summers–Werner: maximal CHSH violation by local observables in spacelike separated regions in the vacuum of free Bose/Fermi fields.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes maximal violation for suitable spacelike separated regions but does not address the long-distance regime.

status_evidence.title: Investigation of the Bell-CHSH inequality in diamond regions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent explicit construction of Weyl-operator test functions in causal diamonds for a massive real scalar field yielding sizeable CHSH violations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work refines explicit violations but does not resolve violation at arbitrarily large separation.

status_evidence.title: Weyl operators, Tomita-Takesaki theory, and Bell-CHSH inequality violations
status_evidence.snippet: Maximal vacuum Bell correlations decay exponentially with the product of the lowest mass and the spacelike separation in massive theories.
status_evidence.claim: Exponential decay bound on maximal violation does not by itself settle whether the violation stays above the classical bound at all distances.
